criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues reputational-harm opinion ($3M) lacks empirical basis
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically challenges Dr. Marchetti’s $3 million reputational-harm opinion as unsupported ipse dixit based on professional experience, noting the absence of studies, surveys, datasets, comparable-company analysis, quantitative model, customer-level data, or replicable derivation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cites FRE 702 for reputational-harm exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion frames the Marchetti expert-opinion exclusions under Rule 702 in Section III.A, and the reputational-harm subsection is one of those challenged opinions, arguing it lacks a reliable foundation and should be excluded.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: References Marchetti's deposition admission on reputational harm
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically states that Dr. Marchetti identified no empirical or quantitative support for the 5–10% customer-loss range and testified it came from her professional experience, citing her deposition at Marchetti Dep. 74:7–76:24. Although it does not include the deposition date, it cites the required admission regarding reputational harm.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges lost-profits regression for excluding FY2020 without sensitivity analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically challenges the $6.78 million lost-profits regression on the ground that Dr. Marchetti excluded FY2020 without testing the effect of including it or quantifying the impact of that exclusion, and frames the issue as an untested exclusion of pandemic-affected data.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Argues lost-profits model ignores Q2 2023 industry downturn
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Dr. Marchetti’s lost-profits model failed to account for the Q2 2023 regional automotive-components downturn, did not benchmark Ridgeline against competitors or assess whether competitors had similar declines, and therefore ignored a confounding industry contraction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References Marchetti's deposition admission on market downturn unawareness
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Dr. Marchetti admitted in deposition that she was unaware of the Q2 2023 regional automotive-components downturn and cites her deposition testimony at 36:10–37:12.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Challenges scrap/rework figure for lack of independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically challenges the $2.34 million scrap-and-rework opinion on the ground that Dr. Marchetti adopted Kevin Cho's internal spreadsheet as the entire quantitative basis and did not verify it against production logs, underlying production records, or audited financial statements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Argues insufficient facts or data under FRE 702
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically argues that Marchetti adopted Kevin Cho’s internal spreadsheet without verification, had no independent basis to confirm the amounts, and states that Rule 703 does not displace Rule 702’s requirement of “sufficient facts” and reliable application. This directly connects the unverified spreadsheet issue to FRE 702’s sufficient facts/data requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies the $11,000 arithmetic discrepancy
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that the five itemized damages amounts total $14,211,000, not the reported $14,200,000, and notes this as a discrepancy. Although it does not spell out '$11,000,' the discrepancy is clearly identified by the stated figures.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Uses arithmetic discrepancy to undermine expert reliability
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion identifies the $11,000 mismatch, notes the expert could not explain it, and uses it within the Rule 702/Daubert section to argue against allowing an unreconciled $14.2 million aggregate as a reliable damages total. Although it says the arithmetic error alone would not warrant exclusion, it connects the discrepancy to the broader reliability challenge rather than merely mentioning it in passing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Argues FRE 407 bars evidence of subsequent remedial measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly cites FRE 407 and argues that Cascade’s November 2023 switch from single-point to three-point moisture sampling and addition of desiccant packets are subsequent remedial measures that should be excluded when offered to prove prior inadequacy, defect, causation, or culpable conduct.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Addresses Plaintiff's anticipated 'feasibility' exception argument
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly anticipates Plaintiff’s feasibility-exception argument under FRE 407 and rebuts it by arguing Cascade has not genuinely controverted feasibility, that asserting prior measures were adequate or industry standard is not the same as claiming alternative precautions were impossible or impracticable, and that the exception should not be used to prove the forbidden inference of prior fault.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Argues OSHA citation should be excluded under FRE 404(b)
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically seeks to exclude the OSHA ventilation citation under Rules 404(b) and 403, identifies Citation No. 2023-OR-00487, and argues Plaintiff wants to use it to show a corporate “pattern” or “culture” of cutting corners, which is impermissible propensity/character evidence under Rule 404(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Argues OSHA citation should be excluded under FRE 403
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly seeks exclusion of the OSHA citation under Rules 404(b) and 403. It states that the citation concerned inadequate ventilation/airborne particulates in Cascade’s Portland blending room and was unrelated to moisture content, resin testing, packaging, or CascadeMax 7200. It then argues any marginal relevance is substantially outweighed by unfair prejudice, jury confusion, and a collateral mini-trial risk.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Addresses Plaintiff's anticipated 'plan or knowledge' argument
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly anticipates Plaintiff’s FRE 404(b) 'knowledge and plan' arguments regarding the OSHA citation and rebuts them by explaining that a ventilation citation has no logical nexus to resin moisture testing, packaging, CascadeMax 7200, or any plan to ship nonconforming resin.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Establishes OSHA citation is unrelated to resin quality
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that the OSHA citation concerned inadequate ventilation and airborne particulate exposure in Cascade's Portland blending room, involving an exhaust fan and filters, and explains that it was unrelated to moisture content, resin testing, packaging, or the CascadeMax 7200 product at issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues Marchetti failed to account for Ridgeline's failure to mitigate
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly raises the mitigation gap: it states Ridgeline discovered the issue on August 22, 2023 but did not order substitute resin until December 11, 2023, and argues Dr. Marchetti performed no analysis of whether earlier procurement would have reduced lost profits or scrap costs. It uses this omission to challenge the reliability of her damages opinions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues lost profits and scrap costs are inflated due to mitigation failure
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly argues that Ridgeline delayed ordering substitute resin after discovering the issue, that Marchetti did not analyze whether earlier procurement would have reduced lost profits or scrap costs, and that her full $6.78 million and $2.34 million figures fail to account for potentially avoidable losses. This connects the damages figures to a mitigation failure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Raises contractual $2M consequential damages cap in FRE 403 context
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly discusses Supply Agreement § 7.2’s consequential-damages exclusion and $2 million cap, identifies Marchetti’s consequential damages categories and amount, and argues that presenting the larger consequential damages figure to the jury would create an anchoring/prejudice risk under Rule 403 unless the cap is addressed first.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies consequential damages categories exceeding cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly identifies that the Supply Agreement caps consequential damages at $2 million and states that Dr. Marchetti classifies $10,292,500 as consequential damages, specifically including lost profits ($6,780,000), replacement resin premium ($512,500), and reputational harm ($3,000,000), which substantially exceeds the cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References untimely defect notice to contextualize damages unreliability
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion states that Ridgeline discovered the issue on August 22, 2023 and gave written notice on September 28, 2023, but it does not characterize the notice as untimely, mention the 37-day delay or 7-day breach of a 30-day contractual notice period, or use the notice delay to contextualize the unreliability or prejudice of Marchetti’s damages opinions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes Marchetti has no prior Daubert qualification in federal court
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion does not mention that Dr. Marchetti has never been qualified as an expert under Daubert in federal court, nor that her prior 30 engagements were limited to state courts or arbitrations, and it does not use that fact to argue for heightened scrutiny.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_004: Applies Federal Rules of Evidence, not Washington evidence rules
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly invokes and applies the Federal Rules of Evidence, including FRE 104, 403, 404(b), 407, 702, and 703, and discusses federal Daubert standards. It does not cite or conflate Washington state evidence rules.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies the court as W.D. Washington
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption states “UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT” and “WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON AT SEATTLE,” which identifies the court as the United States District Court for the Western District of Washington.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies correct parties
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption lists RIDGELINE MANUFACTURING CORP. as Plaintiff and CASCADE POLYMER SOLUTIONS, INC. as Defendant.

criteria_results.title: Caption includes correct case number

criteria_results.title: Motion title identifies it as a motion in limine
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption/title expressly states “DEFENDANT CASCADE POLYMER SOLUTIONS, INC.'S MOTION IN LIMINE TO EXCLUDE...” which clearly identifies the document as a motion in limine.

criteria_results.title: Motion filed on behalf of Cascade (Defendant)
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion caption and title state it is Defendant Cascade Polymer Solutions, Inc.'s motion, the opening paragraph says Defendant Cascade moves, and the signature block identifies counsel as attorneys for Defendant Cascade Polymer Solutions, Inc.

criteria_results.title: Introduction previews Daubert/FRE 702 challenge to Marchetti's testimony
criteria_results.reasoning: The introductory paragraph expressly identifies exclusion of “specified damages opinions of Plaintiff’s expert Dr. Lena Marchetti” as one of the categories of evidence challenged under FRE 702/Daubert-related rules.

criteria_results.title: Introduction previews FRE 407 challenge to subsequent remedial measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion’s introductory paragraph expressly identifies Cascade’s post-dispute testing and packaging changes as a category of evidence to be excluded, and the title also references subsequent remedial measures.

criteria_results.title: Introduction previews FRE 403/404(b) challenge to OSHA citation
criteria_results.reasoning: The introduction states that Cascade moves to exclude, among other categories, “an unrelated OSHA ventilation citation and associated evidence,” and cites Rules 403 and 404(b). This previews the FRE 403/404(b) challenge to the OSHA citation.

criteria_results.title: Includes legal standard section for Daubert/FRE 702
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a 'Governing Standards' section that sets forth FRE 702 requirements, including sufficient facts or data, reliable principles and methods, reliable application, and the preponderance standard. It also expressly references the Court's gatekeeping role under Daubert and discusses reliability.

criteria_results.title: Cites Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion cites Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc., 509 U.S. 579, 589, 592--95 (1993) in the governing standards section.

criteria_results.title: References the Daubert reliability factors
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion discusses the Rule 702/Daubert reliability framework, including sufficient facts or data, reliable principles and methods, reliable application, gatekeeping, analytical gaps, and testability of the expert’s method. This is more than merely citing Daubert by name.

criteria_results.title: Distinct argument section for Daubert/FRE 702 challenge to Marchetti
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a distinct, separately headed argument section: “III.A. Exclude the challenged Marchetti opinions under Rule 702,” with multiple subsections addressing Dr. Marchetti’s opinions and citing Daubert/Rule 702 standards.

criteria_results.title: Distinct argument section for FRE 407 subsequent remedial measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a distinct, separately headed argument section labeled “B. Rule 407 bars evidence of Cascade's post-dispute testing and packaging changes,” which specifically addresses the FRE 407 subsequent remedial measures challenge.

criteria_results.title: Distinct argument section for FRE 403/404(b) OSHA citation
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a distinct, separately headed argument section labeled “C. Exclude the unrelated OSHA citation and associated evidence under Rules 404(b) and 403,” which specifically addresses the OSHA citation evidence under FRE 404(b) and 403.

criteria_results.title: Conclusion requests exclusion of all three categories of evidence
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion includes a clear conclusion section requesting exclusion of specified portions of Dr. Marchetti's expert testimony, evidence concerning Cascade's subsequent testing and packaging changes, and evidence/reference to the OSHA citation and related materials.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states Marchetti's total damages figure as $14.2 million
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Dr. Marchetti offers damages categories “totaling $14.2 million as reported” and refers to the stated aggregate as $14,200,000, satisfying the criterion despite noting an itemized-sum discrepancy.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states lost profits figure as $6,780,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion correctly identifies Dr. Marchetti's lost-profits figure as $6,780,000, including in the damages summary and later argument sections.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states reputational harm figure as $3,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion correctly identifies Dr. Marchetti's reputational-harm/future-business damages figure as $3,000,000, including in the facts section and argument headings.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states scrap/rework figure as $2,340,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion states the scrap and rework damages as "$2,340,000" in the relevant facts section and consistently refers to the same amount as "$2.34 million" elsewhere.

criteria_results.title: Requests alternative relief if full exclusion of Marchetti is denied
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion is not all-or-nothing as to Dr. Marchetti. It seeks exclusion of specific opinion categories individually—reputational harm, lost profits, scrap/rework—and also requests limiting relief, such as precluding her from vouching that the spreadsheet is verified if the scrap/rework opinion is not fully excluded.

criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly references both the OSHA citation number as “2023-OR-00487” and the penalty amount as “$14,502.”

criteria_results.title: Correctly states the consequential damages cap as $2,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that the Supply Agreement caps consequential damages at “$2 million in the aggregate” and later repeats that consequential liability may not exceed “$2 million.”

criteria_results.title: References Marchetti's deposition date of November 18, 2024

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies CascadeMax 7200 as the product at issue
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion expressly states that Ridgeline alleges four “CascadeMax 7200 shipments” contained excess moisture and later refers to “CascadeMax 7200” in connection with the disputed resin quality-control process, correctly identifying the product at issue as CascadeMax 7200 polymer resin.

criteria_results.title: References Dr. Gerhardt's rebuttal report or opinions
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly references the Gerhardt Rebuttal Report multiple times, including in the facts and in support of critiques of Marchetti’s lost-profits and scrap/rework methodologies.
